plain.text: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas spoke in the synagogue so effectively that many Jews and Greeks believed. But some stirred up the Gentiles against them. They stayed a long time, speaking boldly for the Lord, who confirmed his message with signs and wonders. The city was divided. When there was a plot to stone them, they fled to Lystra, Derbe and the surrounding area, and kept preaching the good news.

In Lystra sat a man who had been lame from birth and had never walked. Paul saw that he had faith to be healed and called out, "Stand up on your feet!" The man jumped up and began to walk. The crowd shouted, "The gods have come down to us in human form!" They called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes, and the priest of Zeus brought bulls to offer sacrifices to them. Paul and Barnabas tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd: "Why are you doing this? We too are only human, like you. We are bringing you good news, telling you to turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made the heavens and the earth." God had shown his kindness by giving rain and crops. Even so, they had difficulty stopping the crowd. Then opponents came from Antioch and Iconium, won over the crowd, and stoned Paul, dragging him outside the city, thinking he was dead. But after the disciples gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. The next day he and Barnabas left for Derbe.

They preached the good news in Derbe and won many disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium and Antioch, strengthening the disciples and encouraging them to remain true to the faith. "We must go through many hardships to enter the kingdom of God." They appointed elders in each church and, with prayer and fasting, committed them to the Lord. They sailed back to Antioch, where they had been commended to God's grace. They gathered the church and reported all that God had done through them and how he had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.

summary.bigIdea: Paul and Barnabas keep sharing the good news despite opposition, refuse to be worshipped, and strengthen the new churches.
points: A lame man walks, and the crowd tries to worship Paul and Barnabas as gods.
Paul is stoned and left for dead, but gets up and keeps going.
They appoint elders and report how God opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.
summary.reflection: Paul and Barnabas said, "We too are only men, human like you." How can you point people to God rather than to yourself?
